newsitem.title: USA: Hewlett-Packard slips after analyst meeting.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett-Packard slips after analyst meeting.

text.p: Shares of Hewlett-Packard Co. slipped after analysts emerged from a meeting with senior executives in New York on Thursday saying there were few new developments and the company's tone was cautious.
"There was no real incremental news," one trader said after the meeting broke up. "They tried to put a positive spin on the second half (of the company's fiscal year)."
HP shares were down 1-1/4 at 52-3/4 in late exchange trade.
Analysts said HP Chairman and CEO Lewis Platt's message was cautious although he has more favorable comparisons in the fiscal second half when performance was weak a year ago.

But analysts and traders said little emerged from the meeting that would prompt them to change earnings estimates beyond what was said in the company's second quarter conference call a week ago, after HP disappointed Wall Street with eight percent revenue growth and a slow three percent rise in orders.
Fully 18 of the 20 analysts polled by First Call have already reduced their fiscal 1997 estimates in the last week and 15 analysts also pared their fiscal 1998 estimates.
"All I can tell you is that Lew was comfortable that this too will pass," said ABN AMRO Chicago Corp analyst David Wu.

"He obviously has been there before -- he's been behind the 8-ball before," added Wu, who a year ago downgraded the stock after the company's blockbuster fiscal 1996 second quarter and who upgraded his rating on HP to a "buy" last week on the view Wall Street was under-valuing HP's second half potential.

"The numbers he had in the first half of last year were artifically high, the numbers he's getting in the first half of this year they were articially low," Wu said. "I think Lew's going to come back. I'll bet on his company. I think his business is stronger than it looks at first glance."

A spokeswoman for Hewlett-Packard, which reshuffled senior management in its computer group earlier this week and was announcing new high-end computers later in the day, said HP had reported no significant new developments at the meeting.
